t.1.192.2: The great-souled one by whom that bow was drawn and the target pierced is Arjuna, best of victors, bearer of the great bow and arrows.
t.1.192.1: Then the kings' trusted spies brought them the news: the fair Draupadī had been united with the Pāṇḍavas as her husbands.
t.1.192.3: He who, mighty, lifted up Śalya, king of the Madras, and whirled him around, and who, enraged, terrified the men in battle with a tree.
t.1.192.5: Then, when they heard that those who bore the guise of brahmins were the Kaunteyas, the sons of King Pāṇḍu, amazement arose among the lords of men.
t.1.192.4: Nor was there any alarm at all in that great-souled one there; he was Bhīma, terrible to encounter, who struck down the limbs of enemy hosts.
t.1.192.6: For Kuntī, together with her sons, was formerly heard to have been burned in the lac house; so all the kings regard them as men born again.
t.1.192.7: Then, crying shame upon Bhīṣma and upon Dhṛtarāṣṭra the Kaurava, on account of the exceedingly cruel deed that Purocana had done,
t.1.192.8: When the svayaṃvara was over, all those kings went back the way they had come, having learned that the Pāṇḍavas had been chosen.
t.1.192.9: Then King Duryodhana, dejected, together with his brothers, with Aśvatthāman, with his maternal uncle, with Karṇa and with Kṛpa,
t.1.192.10: Having turned back after seeing Śvetavāhana chosen by Draupadī, Duḥśāsana, abashed, spoke to him slowly, as if very haltingly.
t.1.192.11: If that man were not a brahmin, he would not have won Draupadī; for no one, O king, truly knows him to be Dhanaṃjaya.
t.1.192.12: I consider fate supreme and human effort fruitless. Shame on our efforts, father, for the Pāṇḍavas are still alive here!
t.1.192.13: Speaking thus among themselves and reviling Purocana, they entered Hāstinapura, dejected and bereft of their senses.
t.1.192.14: Frightened and robbed of their resolve, they saw the mighty Pārthas freed from the fire and allied with Drupada.
t.1.192.15: And having thought of Dhṛṣṭadyumna, and likewise of Śikhaṇḍin, and of the other sons of Drupada, all skilled in every kind of warfare,
t.1.192.16: Then Vidura, having heard that the Pāṇḍavas had been chosen by Draupadī, and that the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra had returned ashamed, their pride broken,
t.1.192.17: Then, O lord of the people, the Kṣattṛ, his heart gladdened and filled with wonder, said to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, "By good fortune the Kurus prosper!"
t.1.192.19: For the king, whose eyes are wisdom, believes through lack of knowledge that his eldest son Duryodhana has been chosen by the daughter of Drupada.
t.1.192.18: But the king, the son of Vicitravīrya, having heard those words of Vidura, spoke with the greatest delight, O Bhārata: "What good fortune! What good fortune!"
t.1.192.20: Then he ordered a wealth of ornaments for Draupadī, and commanded his son Duryodhana, "Let Kṛṣṇā be brought here!"
t.1.192.21: Then afterward Vidura told him that it was the Pāṇḍavas who had been chosen, all of them heroes, safe and well and honored by Drupada, and he told him also of their many other kinsmen, endowed with strength.
t.1.192.22: Just as they are Pāṇḍu's sons, so, and even more, are they mine. This, Vidura, I deem my surpassing joy and prosperity: that the heroic Pāṇḍavas are safe and well and have won allies.
t.1.192.24: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: To him, speaking thus, Vidura replied, "May this mind of yours remain always so, O king, for a hundred years."
t.1.192.23: For what king, O Kṣattṛ, even one whose fortune has departed, having gained Drupada and his kinsmen as a friend, would not, longing for prosperity, wish to rise and thrive?
t.1.192.25: Then, O lord of the people, Duryodhana and Rādheya approached Dhṛtarāṣṭra and spoke these words to him.
t.1.192.26: In the presence of Vidura we two cannot speak to you, O king. Now that we are alone, we shall say it: what is this that you wish to do?
t.1.192.28: When one thing ought to be done, O king, you do another, O sinless one; for their strength must constantly be broken, my son.
t.1.192.27: That you, father, regard the growth of your rivals as your own growth, and that you sing their praises in the presence of the Kṣattṛ, O best of men…
t.1.192.29: So we are deliberating on what should be done now that the time has come, so that they may not devour us along with our sons, armies, and kinsmen.
